title: Export every Frame string column to Arrow as large_string
description:
A `Frame` string column now always exports to Arrow as `large_string`. Previously the type depended on how the frame was held: a frame built with `Frame.from_arrow()` or received below the shared-memory size floor exported `string`, while a region-backed one exported `large_string`.

Also vendors libmizu #15, so `Frame.from_arrow()` copies a null-free `large_string` column in bulk rather than element by element.

title: Skip string walks for frame columns sent by reference
description:
Re-sending a received `Frame` after a round trip through an Arrow consumer such as `pa.table(frame)` no longer walks string columns that are sent back unchanged. Those columns cross by reference, so the walk was wasted work.

For a 5M-row frame with a string column, an unchanged re-send goes from 1.1 ms (2.8 ms with nulls) to 0.002 ms, and a re-send with one computed column from 1.8 ms to 0.6 ms.

This vendors libmizu shikokuchuo/libmizu#14, which adds the lazy Arrow open the frame stage now uses.

title: Refresh the stdlib comparison benchmark tables
description:
Updates the benchmark tables in the README and docs from a fresh run of `benchmarks/mizu-stdlib-bench.py`:

* The 8 KB vector round trip is now 2.0 µs (was 2.4 µs) and the parallel map 2.8 ms (was 2.9 ms).
* Pipelined throughput is now 2,200,000 tasks/s (was 2,390,000), the best measured in this run.
* The `ProcessPoolExecutor` pipelined and `ThreadPoolExecutor` map figures are updated, and the speedups recomputed.

The run is recorded in `benchmarks/notes.md`, and the docs freeze cache is regenerated.

title: Vendor libmizu batch wake: one worker per task
description:
Updates the vendored libmizu to current main and moves the pin to match.

* `Pool.submit_batch()` now wakes at most one idle worker per task. Previously a short batch woke every idle worker in the pool, and could wake the same worker more than once.

* On an idle 8-worker pool, a one-task batch wakes 1 worker rather than about 9, and the `submit_batch()` call drops from 48.5 to 20.7 us. Large-batch throughput is unchanged.

Also records the benchmark run and new best rows in `benchmarks/notes.md`.

title: Stop idle workers importing the map module
description:
The first task on a new pool no longer waits while an idle worker loads numpy.

A worker's idle hook imported `pymizu._map`, and numpy with it, the first time the worker parked, so the first task queued behind a ~25 ms import. The hook now does nothing until a map has loaded that module.

First task on a fresh pool (builtin task, minimum of 12):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 4 workers | 11.6 ms | 0.03 ms |
| 1 worker | 22.0 ms | 0.03 ms |

A new test checks that an idle worker has not loaded the map module.

title: Recurse the compact codec into nested containers
description:
Nested lists, tuples, and dicts sent between Python processes now cross in the compact binary form instead of falling back to pickle. On the benchmark tree (a 64-key dict of mixed lists) a channel send drops from 13.8 to about 10 us.

A payload that references the same list or dict more than once, including a cyclic one, still crosses as a pickle, so sharing is preserved. Nesting deeper than 500 levels and containers over 64 elements also keep the pickle path.

Both ends need this version: an older pymizu fails the receive of a nested payload with "corrupt payload slot".

title: Optimize spec-stream map workers
description:
Memoize source-spec compilation and keep single-morsel runner contexts private, so spec-stream chunks no longer retain completed regions on Python workers. Nested runner dispatch now reuses its resolved context.

Adds regression tests, report-only benchmark rows, and a changelog entry. Local 256-chunk A/B probes improved from 4.4 to 2.5 ms for trivial source specs and from 7.1–7.3 to 2.5 ms for prefix-plus-tail sources.

title: Add Channel.recv_batch_async()
description:
Adds `Channel.recv_batch_async()` to receive a burst of channel messages as one list on one `asyncio.Future`.

Ensures batch receives return a list even when `n = 1`, with regression tests and updated documentation.

title: Eliminate spec-stream map copies
description:
Template chunks in a spec stream now gather directly into the final accumulator via the new internal `_map_gather_into()`, removing the temporary chunk array and second memcpy.

Also fixes `Pool.map()` with a multi-element template raising `TypeError` during collection when numpy is unavailable.

title: Skip cancellation on clean map collects and close one-shot regions
description:
A clean map collect no longer runs the cancellation cleanup (all task handles are already consumed by then), and a non-prepared map collected with collect="copy" now releases its shared memory immediately rather than at GC — resident memory across 16 back-to-back 1M-element maps stays flat instead of growing ~250 MB.

Timeout, error, explicit cancellation, worker-death, and prepared-map behavior are unchanged. A late runner opening its region after the unlink fails harmlessly into its already-cancelled task.

title: Make cancel() on a collected map handle a no-op
description:
Calling `cancel()` on a map handle that had already been collected could disrupt a later run of the same prepared map: the later run returned `None` in place of its results, with no error.

`cancel()` now does nothing once a handle's collect has finished. Cancelling a map while its collect is still in progress works as before.

title: Drop Python 3.10 support (minimum 3.11)
description:
pymizu now requires Python 3.11 or later, following Python 3.10's end of life in October 2026. pip on Python 3.10 continues to install pymizu 0.1.1, the last release that supports it.

* Drops 3.10 from the CI matrix and the wheel builds, and moves the ruff and pyrefly targets to 3.11.
* Annotates self-returning methods with `typing.Self`, so `Channel.create()`, `Pool.create()`, `Pool.attach()`, `PoolExecutor.create()`, and `Frame.from_arrow()` report the right return type for subclasses.

There is no 3.10-specific code to remove: the remaining version-dependent paths in the C extension are already gated on 3.12 and 3.13.

title: pymizu 0.1.1
description: Finalizes the 0.1.1 changelog and vendors the merged libmizu 0.2.0 revision (6e5571185385936ff33aa9416657a7280fead105). Versioning stays tag-derived via setuptools_scm; no static version is added.

title: Elide the channel batch-receive API
description:
Removes the three unreleased batch methods — `recv_batch_async()`, `iter_batches()`, and `iter_batches_async()` — along with their tests, docs, and changelog entry, so the next release can ship as a patch.

The underlying plumbing (the C `recv_batch` verb and the `_aio.py` drain paths) stays in place, and the sync `recv_batch()` from 0.1.0 is untouched. Reverting this one commit reinstates the feature in full.

title: Fix sdist tests and guard PyPI publishing
description:
This fixes two release-path issues:

- Runs the shipped tests from an unpacked sdist, skipping the docs-reference check when its checkout-only configuration is absent.
- Restricts production PyPI publishing to tag pushes, so manually dispatching a tag remains a dry run.

Validated with the full unpacked-sdist suite (1168 passed, 2 skipped), Ruff, Pyrefly, and actionlint.

title: Remove dead code, fold duplicated paths and re-vendor libmizu
description:
Removes code found by a redundancy scan of pymizu and libmizu. No behaviour or API change.

* Deletes dead code: two uncalled functions, a struct field and a plan array that were written but never read, an unreachable branch pair in the same-language frame stage, and the superseded `Task._async_set()` (its one test now uses `_tasks_enroll()`).
* Folds duplicates: three copies of the `[i,j]` path walk into one, three copies of the two-pass bytes writer into one, and `Pool.stats()` onto the row builders `Pool.dump()` already uses.
* Uses `PyModule_AddFunctions()` for the map and layout verbs, and a table for the lazy re-exports in `pymizu.__getattr__()`.
* Re-vendors libmizu at shikokuchuo/libmizu#9, which folds the collect wait loops, the POSIX region opens and the notify arm.

The full test suite passes, and `benchmarks/mizu-bench.py` shows no regression against main over five alternating runs.

title: Remove the TestPyPI publish leg
description:
The TestPyPI dry run existed to prove the trusted-publishing path before the first release. With pymizu now on PyPI, that proof has happened for real, so this drops the leg: the `testpypi` dispatch input and `publish-testpypi` job in publish.yml, the `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_OVERRIDES_FOR_PYMIZU` plumbing through cibuildwheel's `environment-pass`, and the matching AGENTS.md notes.

The plain `workflow_dispatch` dry run (full matrix, no upload) stays for validating before tagging.

title: Improve executor performance
description:
* `PoolExecutor.map()` now supports `chunksize` and `buffersize`, with lazy input consumption and bounded pending work.
* `PoolExecutor.submit()` waits for result-slot capacity instead of raising `SlotsExhaustedError`.
* Optional imports now load on first use, and `Pool.stop()` no longer waits an extra 50 ms after workers exit cleanly.

title: Send region-backed Frame task arguments by name
description:
A `Frame` received from a pool or channel is backed by a shared-memory region. Passing one to `Pool.submit()` used to rewrite it into a fresh region, and a second such argument sent the whole task to pickle.

* A region-backed `Frame` argument now crosses by its region's name. It takes no staging checkout, so a task can carry several, alongside a large buffer.
* The submit pins the task's arguments until a worker claims the task, so the region cannot be recycled while the name is in flight.
* No wire change: the existing frame leaf with a zero aux is the by-name form.

Also fixes sending a `Frame` taken from a list or dict received from an R peer, where the peer received the whole container and not the one frame. Only a frame that is its region's root now goes by name.

title: Speed up Frame.from_arrow copies and send Frame task arguments by name
description:
This PR makes two things faster and fixes one bug. It replaces #45.

## Faster `Frame.from_arrow()`

When the Arrow input has more than one chunk, or is sliced, `Frame.from_arrow()` has to copy each column. Several column types were copied one row at a time. They are now copied one chunk at a time:

* date, timestamp and duration columns
* dictionary columns with int32 indices
* uint64 columns
* string (utf8) columns with no nulls

String columns with nulls, `large_utf8` and `string_view` columns are unchanged.

This needs two new functions from libmizu, so the vendored copy is updated to shikokuchuo/libmizu#8.

## Faster `Pool.submit()` with a received `Frame`

A `Frame` that you receive from a pool or a channel lives in shared memory. Passing one to `Pool.submit()` used to copy it into a new shared-memory region. Passing two in one task copied and pickled both.

Such a `Frame` is now passed by reference: the worker opens the same shared memory. A task can take any number of them. The data stays alive until a worker has picked up the task, even if you drop your own `Frame` first.

## Bug fix

If an R peer sent a list of data frames, and you sent one of those frames on by itself, the receiver got the whole list. It now gets the one frame.

title: Re-vendor libmizu Arrow null handling speedups
description:
Re-vendors the libmizu core at shikokuchuo/libmizu#6 and shikokuchuo/libmizu#7.

* Sending an Arrow table with a factor (dictionary) column is faster.

* Sending Arrow columns where many values are nulls is faster, especially long all-null stretches.

* Sending a table made of several batches or sliced batches that contains nulls is faster.

title: Speed up foreign Frame sends
description:
Foreign `Frame` sends now use the cached Arrow export and core frame writer, so large frames take the shared-memory region path instead of a second by-value copy.

Custom row names and R attributes are preserved, and complex columns keep their by-value fallback. Redundant Arrow staging state is removed, with regression coverage for the new paths.

The 2M-row float/string benchmark now takes 1.43 ms, matching a direct `pa.Table` send (previously about 9 ms).

title: Re-vendor libmizu Arrow conversion kernels
description:
Re-vendors libmizu from main for faster Arrow columns with scattered nulls, dictionary columns, and temporal values.

The full pymizu suite passes, including the R interop tests.

title: Fix Arrow RecordBatch and vector staging
description:
Fixes sending `pyarrow.RecordBatch`, `pyarrow.StructArray`, and nanoarrow struct arrays to R peers.

Unifies Arrow staging so each producer is exported once per send. Bare vectors no longer inherit the frame-only row limit, and region-sized record batches now have regression coverage.

title: Defer package version lookup until first access
description: Package metadata is now loaded only when `pymizu.__version__` is accessed, then cached for later use. This cuts median warm `import pymizu` time by about 32% (31.1 ms to 21.2 ms), with the existing missing-metadata fallback unchanged.

title: Speed up small task collections
description:
This PR avoids a heap allocation for collections of up to 16 tasks by storing their task words inline. Larger collections continue to use the existing heap fallback.

Small `Pool.collect_any()` and `Pool.collect_all()` calls are now a few nanoseconds faster. Includes boundary and error-path tests for 16 and 17 tasks.

title: Speed up C boundary calls
description: Speeds up C verb boundary calls, pickle reads, and NumPy calls while preserving CPython-compatible keyword handling. Also trims 1-D NumPy shape allocation and refreshes the benchmark results and documentation.

title: Resolve task fns through sys.modules; drop the fn caches
description:
Workers now resolve task functions through `sys.modules` first, falling back to the full import machinery only on a first-ever import. Both per-worker fn-resolution caches go: after the faster miss path their marginal value is noise, and removing them retires the stale-rebind semantics — a callable replaced in an already-imported module is now picked up on the next submission.

The single-fn round-trip rows are flat within their bands; tasks crossing many distinct functions gain 12–27% (A/B probes in benchmarks/notes.md).

title: Build with pinned -O3, LTO, and hidden visibility; strip release wheels
description:
Pins optimization flags and enables link-time optimization for all builds.

* POSIX builds now compile with `-O3 -DNDEBUG -fvisibility=hidden -flto` (compile and link), removing dependence on each CI image's sysconfig defaults. The extension's dynamic exports drop from 310 symbols to just `PyInit__pymizu`.
* Windows clang-cl builds use `/clang:-O3 /clang:-flto=thin` and link with lld-link, since MS link.exe cannot consume thin-LTO bitcode.
* Release wheels get the same flags via cibuildwheel's environment and are stripped at link on manylinux and macOS.

Verified on macOS arm64: full suite green including the cross-language legs (1130 pass, 1 skip), back-to-back A/B against the previous build within run-to-run noise (details in benchmarks/notes.md), ruff + pyrefly clean. The Windows wheel build is being validated by a publish.yml dry run on this branch.

title: Faster large frame relay and batch task collection
description:
* Adopts libmizu's batch-collect verb (`mizu_pool_collect_terminal`) in the executor drain and the asyncio pump; large bursts of outstanding futures resolve faster.
* The spill layer keeps one over-cap (64 MB+) region per handle, so relaying a large frame no longer creates a fresh shared-memory region per send (~4x on the 80 MB relay row).
* Vendors libmizu 7b42311; the changelog's Unreleased section is consolidated; records in benchmarks/notes.md.

title: Fix PoolExecutor submit/drain collect race
description:
Fixes a rare race where a `PoolExecutor` future failed with "task handle already collected" when a task finished as it was submitted: submit's inline resolve and the listener's drain pass could both claim the one result slot, and the loser was resolved with a spurious error.

A terminal-at-submit task no longer enters the executor's outstanding set, so no drain pass can claim its slot ahead of the inline collect. The redundant per-submit lock is folded into the one condition lock, dropping one acquire per submit.

title: Speed up small-container sends, frame resends, and view Arrow exports
description:
* The compact codec's size and write passes fuse into one validating walk; the writer's exact bytes are pinned by a new `_codec_stream` hook, a compat contract for version-mixed pools. Small list round trips ~-11%.
* A `pymizu.Frame` caches its stage construction at the first same-language send, so repeated sends skip the export rebuild, fresh mapping, and provenance round-trip (~-10% heap-backed resends).
* The clean validity verdict memoizes on `_MapOutView` and `_ShmView`: re-exports like `pa.array(view)` skip the sentinel scan (~40x).
* Review follow-ups: the frame stage's small arrays go stack-resident, dict sizing is one call, and a >4 GiB str/bytes container leaf now falls back to pickle instead of sending a corrupt stream.

title: Speed up task decode, spin waits, and buffer task staging
description:
* Workers cache task-function resolution: repeated `Pool.submit()` of the same callable, and `pymizu.call()` spec tasks, skip the per-task module import. A function rebound in an already-imported module is no longer picked up by a worker that has run it — restart workers with `retire()` / `spawn_workers()`, or use cloudpickle.
* The interrupt-check hook is throttled to 1 ms per thread, for faster `spin=True` channel waits.
* Task frames negotiate buffer arguments (e.g. numpy arrays) once per leaf instead of twice, and keep the views on the stack for small tasks.
* Small map results keep their leaf plans on the stack, and the map-result publish cleanup walks only initialized plans.

Worker-decode-bound rows roughly double (pipelined pool batch 4.09M, `collect_all_async` 3.67M, 64 waiters 3.44M — three new best-knowns); pool round-trip -19%, spec round-trip ~-30%, buffer tasks -9%; submitter-bound and control rows flat. Records in benchmarks/notes.md.

title: Speed up send staging, map loops, and asyncio waiter detach
description:
* Sends: module probes no longer raise on a miss, exact `bytes` skip the buffer negotiation, and template maps with numpy scalar results no longer acquire a buffer per element.
* Maps: streaming chunks index their slice directly instead of through a per-element lambda, and seeded maps hash the seed once per batch instead of once per element. Results stay byte-identical, pinned by new tests.
* Asyncio: cancelling a pending receive is now O(1) instead of a queue scan, and enrollment no longer allocates a closure per waiter.

Cancelling waiters is ~4x faster, `recv_async` is 27% faster, streaming maps are ~6% faster. The benchmark records live in `benchmarks/notes.md`.

title: Linux performance pass and vendored libmizu update
description:
Brings in libmizu 11fbeca (shikokuchuo/libmizu#3) plus the binding-side findings from the same Linux tuning plan.

- Re-vendor: masked Arrow sends to R peers 704 -> 344 us (f64), and large zero-copy views prefault their pages on Linux.
- A Frame's Arrow export no longer re-scans every column for nulls on each send when a previous scan found none: repeated sends of the same null-free frame drop 25.8 -> 14.8 ms on the 10-col relay row.
- The benchmark suite pins OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1: OpenBLAS's spinning thread pool was swinging the pipelined rows by ~30% on few-core hosts.

Full suite 1092 passed, 12 skipped; ruff and format clean; benchmarks/notes.md records the Linux baseline and A/B.

title: Add Channel.recv_batch_async() and batch iterators
description:
Adds the async counterpart of `recv_batch()`, plus batch stream forms for sync and async consumers.

- `Channel.recv_batch_async(n)` resolves one Future with a burst of up to `n` messages as one list — short when fewer have arrived, never waiting to fill. It shares the FIFO with `recv_async()` singles in call order, follows `recv_batch()`'s decline rules, and caps at one drain quantum (2048) per pass.
- `Channel.iter_batches()` and `Channel.iter_batches_async()` iterate over received batches until the channel closes — the batch forms of the channel iterators.

Includes tests, channels-guide examples, and changelog entries.

title: Fix async pool collections hanging when a pool is reused across event loops
description:
Using `Pool.collect_any_async()`, `Pool.collect_all_async()`, or `await` on a map across more than one event loop — for example back-to-back `asyncio.run()` calls on one pool — could hang forever. A task's wake fired against the closed previous loop, or while the waiter was enrolling on a stale arm, was lost with no way to recover, and the wait never finished.

Enrollments now re-check whenever the arm (re-)captures a loop, and a wake that cannot deliver its drain releases the coalescing flag instead of absorbing every later signal.

Adds two regression tests that reproduce both hangs deterministically; the asyncio cross-language hammer now runs 400 iterations clean (previously hung within the first few).

title: Stage top-level scalars directly as 'I' tags on foreign handles
description:
Sends of top-level bool, int, float, and complex scalars to R peers now write the interchange scalar bytes directly at the staging gate, instead of walking the general interchange writer. The bytes on the wire are identical; only the path is shorter, so scalar-heavy R-bound sends are faster.

The same-language path is unchanged, and an int past int64 still raises the same `DeclinedError`.

title: Speed up Task.collect_async() and PoolExecutor submits
description:
`Task.collect_async()` and `await task` are much faster for tasks that finish between awaits: an already-published result now resolves end to end in C with no arm cycle and no Python frame, the pool pump's arm is sticky instead of re-arming per await, and enrollment probes terminal before arming and re-checks the new entry only. The single-task waiters live in a C registry scanned once per wake.

`PoolExecutor` submits are faster in synchronous use, particularly with many outstanding futures: the submit fuses submit + announce + terminal re-check into one C call and resolves a finished task inline with no drain pass, and the drain's scan-and-collect is one call.

Same-host A/B: pool collect_async 522.6k → 1,592.0k tasks/s; executor wrap_future rows +31–37%; executor sync 5.38 → 4.8 µs/task; collect_all_async and channel rows flat. The 64-waiters row dips ~7%: the old per-enrollment full-set pump hid settle work inside the burst; the new enrollments defer it to 2–3 wake passes. Details in benchmarks/notes.md.

title: Speed up the unseeded map element loop
description:
The worker-side element loop in `Pool.map()` no longer pays a closure call and a `*args/**kwargs` unpack per element. The unseeded path now runs one try around the loop — the element-index error annotation is unchanged — and calls `fn(get(i))` directly when no extra arguments ride along (122 -> 72 ns/elt in-process). A fresh profile showed a C batch loop could remove nothing further: the residual is numpy scalar creation plus the user's fn call, which C cannot accelerate without numpy headers.

Trivial map: 0.070 -> 0.056 us/elt; template: 0.054 -> 0.034; prepared: 0.064 -> 0.049; winsum x 20000: 734k -> 759k tasks/s. Seed and skew rows are flat by design (full A/B in `benchmarks/notes.md`).

Stacked on #22: based on `perf/map-result-codec`.

title: Send Pool.map() results over a typed result codec instead of pickle
description:
`Pool.map()` results no longer pass through pickle on the way back from the workers. Runner and chunk publishes now ride a new typed frame: each batch crosses as raw bytes and is rebuilt on collect as exact Python or numpy scalar classes (tuples of them included). Batches outside the typed subset (a mid-batch type change, an int past int64, bools, strings, `None`) keep the pickle form, and an R host driving Python workers through a spec map receives the same plain objects as before.

Trivial map (numpy x): 0.375 -> 0.069 us/elt. winsum x 2000: 497k -> 689k tasks/s; x 20000: 498k -> 738k. The Python-float and template rows are flat (full A/B in `benchmarks/notes.md`).

title: Gate streaming spec seed offsets and inform numpy-less complex map errors
description:
- A map over a complex `x` or a complex template staged by an R host died on a worker or collector without numpy with a bare `KeyError: 15`. The three numpy-less readers now raise an informative `TypeError` naming numpy instead.
- `Pool.map(stream=True)` on R workers silently derived wrong per-element RNG streams when the seed offset plus `len(x)` exceeded 2^53 (R seeks element offsets in doubles). The seed is now declined at the call site, matching mizu's own guard; same-language pools are unaffected since Python composes offsets in exact integers.

title: Faster masked int64 Arrow conversions to R peers
description:
Re-vendors libmizu 6dfe375, which fuses the masked conversion's genuine-sentinel count into the element copy instead of a second pass over the output.

Sends of masked int32 and int64 Arrow columns to R peers are faster — the int64 path, which previously paid the count the float64 path never does, now matches it.

Same-host A/B: masked int64 185.6 → ~140 µs/send (the int64:int32 gap ~1.5× → ~1.1×). No wire or ABI change.

title: De-thread pymizu from _map.py and dedup its Python structure
description:
* `_map.py` imports `pymizu` once at module level instead of threading it through `Map._open_*`/`_collect`/`_resolve`, `_stream_fail`, `_collect_region`, and both stream windows (cycle-safe: `_get_map()` imports it lazily).
* `PreparedMap` drops its 8 mirrored `_Plan` slots and reads `self._plan.*` directly.
* New single homes: `Map._gate()` for the collect gates, `_stream_window_params()` for the streaming geometry, `_cancel_capsules()`/`_cancel_tasks()`/`_take_view()` for the cancel/cleanup paths, `_quantum_hit()` and `_settle_via_loop()` in `_aio.py`.
* Stream windows carry `spec` as a class attribute; `Pool.starmap` skips the list copy when x is already a list.
* `_pymizu.pyi` gains the test-seam exports, `_map_stage`'s fixed signature, and the dynamically-set exception attributes.

title: Deduplicate repeated C idioms
description: Consolidates duplicated C idioms across the extension sources into shared helpers, and fixes a latent double-free on frame_rebuild's OOM path. A/B bench run against main shows parity.

title: Hot-path efficiency
description:
- The 'I' walker records a compact path segment per descent and renders the decline path string only when a decline happens, instead of formatting per element.
- The frame writer's masked-column gate reads the recorded null count rather than re-scanning the validity bitmap.
- The MIZL write pass records each remote leaf's validity claim as it writes, dropping the third element walk.
- The Channel/Pool facades cache their hot bound C verbs, and the lazy `_aio`/`_map` imports and raw-handle stashes ride module-global holders.

Benchmark evidence is in the `benchmarks/notes.md` entry, with the four plan-k rows in the best-known table updated.

title: Fix a Pool.stop deadlock with an in-flight notify drain
description: Stopping a pool could hang forever when an executor drain was in flight on the notify listener thread: the stop gate parked the callback while the core's watch stop waited for it. The gate now answers the callback with the closed handle instead, so the drain unwinds and the stop completes.

title: Refactor C near the byte-identity surface
description:
* The ten vector-body emit arms in interop.c share one reserve/done bracket instead of hand-inlined capacity checks.
* layout.c's five size/write blob pairs collapse into dual-form single functions, so a size pass can no longer drift from its write pass.
* The factor/Date/POSIXct/difftime attribute gates are single-sourced across the four read paths, keeping the wire shapes the R package mirrors in exactly one place.
* The three codec container readers merge behind one reader parameterized on the leaf function and dict-key enforcement.
* The two pinned-payload sends share one bracket helper.

title: Cache numpy entry points and trim small redundancies
description: Mechanical, behaviour-preserving cleanups.

title: pymizu 0.1.0
description: Closes #13.

title: Make the pytest config a bit more strict
description:
This PR adds `--strict-config`, `xfail_strict = true`, and `minversion = "8.0"` to `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`. And we also switch `addopts` to list form. With `--strict-config`, a misspelled setting in the pytest table becomes an error instead of being silently ignored, the same way `--strict-markers` already treats marker typos.

`xfail_strict` makes an `xfail` test that starts passing count as a failure, so the marker gets removed once the bug is fixed. I know that there are no xfails today (so nothing changes now) but this is good for when they may be eventually added. The `dev` extra gets a matching `pytest>=8` floor. Finally, the Testing section of `AGENTS.md` is updated to describe these new settings.

title: ci: add package-level tests for `__all__` and `__version__`
description:
This PR adds `tests/test_package.py`, covering the package as a whole rather than in any one module. Using `test_version_is_set()` with `__version__` resolves from installed metadata rather than the `"0.0.0"`/`PackageNotFoundError` fallback (a pattern I use all the time).

`test_public_api()` with `set(pymizu.__all__)` equals an explicit set of names (grouped by the same sections as the API reference in `docs/great-docs.yml`), so a change to the public API needs a deliberate edit here that shows up in review. Before this PR only `PreparedMap` was checked (with `test_facade.py`).
 
With `test_public_api_names_exist()` every name in `__all__` resolves (including the lazy `Map` / `PreparedMap` / `DimArray` re-exports) the same way `from pymizu import *` resolves them.

title: Integration into `asyncio` event loop
description:
- Async maps
- Event-driven async

title: Add a CI diagnostic for the R-side pymizu probe on the 3.14 leg
Adapt the frame-export tests to polars 2.0's stream ingest
description:
Fixes main's CI after the polars 2.0.0 release.

`pl.from_arrow()` on a stream-only Arrow producer now returns a `struct Series` instead of a `DataFrame` ([breaking change](https://docs.pola.rs/releases/upgrade/2/)).

Full suite green on polars 2.0.0 and 1.44.2.

title: Add streaming Pool.map with stream = TRUE
description:
Closes #6.

Adds `stream = TRUE` to `Pool.map()` and `Pool.map_prepare()`. A streaming map never writes the whole of `x` to shared memory. It sends fixed slices of `x` to the workers as they take work, under a sliding submit/collect window. Shared-memory use stays bounded by the window times the slice size, not by `sizeof(x)`.

* Results, ordering, `template`, `collect`, `seed` invariance, and the error taxonomy are unchanged.
* The chunk count defaults to `min(len(x), 32 * live workers)`, and `chunks=` overrides it outright.
* A `pymizu.call()` spec as `fn` raises `TypeError`: streaming needs same-language workers.
* A streaming prepared map re-slices a replacement `x` of any shape, and restages into a fresh region after an unclean run.
* A `collect_any`/`collect_all` position stamp no longer overwrites a map error's element index.
* The R binding ships the same feature as `.stream = TRUE`, with the same semantics.

Checks: the full test suite (448 tests) passes, and ruff and pyrefly are clean. Cross-language map tests pass against the matching mizu build. Benchmark rows hold their bands, and the validation runs confirm the footprint model: 6.3% of the region path's shared memory for a 16 MB `x`, against the model's 6.2%.

title: Silence the test suite's expected warnings
description:
Three fixes keep the test output quiet:

- The intentional conversion warning in `test_cvt_warning_raises_after_the_spilled_write` is now detected with `pytest.warns`.
- NaT scalars and additions carry explicit units, so NumPy no longer raises its generic-unit deprecation.
- The corpus generator's expected float-to-int warnings run under `np.errstate`.

The full suite runs with zero warnings.

title: Add a process-wide default pool
description:
Adds three functions: `default_pool()`, `set_default_pool()`, and `using_pool()`.

A package can now read a default pool that the user sets for the whole session. The setter returns the previous default, so callers can save and restore it. The context manager restores the previous default on exit. The default never overrides `current_pool()` inside a task.

Closes #3.
